pages.text:
Product Pricing Guides Docs Theme
Docs Home
On this page
Available Integrations
Getting Started
Connect from an agent, the CLI, or the API
Integrations
Cronitor integrates with popular communication and incident management platforms to ensure your team stays informed when monitors detect issues. These integrations can be added to Notification Lists and reused across multiple monitors.
Agents connected to the Cronitor MCP server can list, create, and connect integrations without seeing their secrets.
Available Integrations
Detailed setup instructions for popular integrations:
Service Description
Slack Send alerts to channels or direct messages with rich formatting and action buttons
Microsoft Teams Deliver alerts to Teams channels with embedded monitor details and quick actions
Discord Post formatted alerts to Discord servers with customizable webhooks
Google Chat Send alerts to Google Workspace Chat spaces using webhooks
Telegram Receive alerts via Telegram bot in direct messages or group chats
Lark Deliver alerts to LarkSuite channels using custom bot integrations
PagerDuty Create incidents with automatic escalation, on-call routing, and resolution tracking
Datadog On-Call Route Cronitor alerts to a Datadog On-Call team for escalation and incident response
OpsGenie Trigger OpsGenie alerts with intelligent routing and escalation policies
Splunk On-Call Route alerts through Splunk On-Call with timeline integration and team coordination
Webhooks Send custom HTTP requests to any endpoint with flexible payload formatting
Getting Started
To set up integrations:
Navigate to Settings > Integrations in your Cronitor dashboard
Select the service you want to connect
Follow the setup instructions for your chosen platform
Add the integration to your Notification Lists
Attach notification lists to your monitors to start receiving alerts
Once configured, these integrations will automatically send alerts when your monitors detect issues and recovery notifications when they return to healthy status.
Connect from an agent, the CLI, or the API
Every integration can be connected without the dashboard:
How it connects Services
Browser authorization Slack, PagerDuty
API key or webhook URL Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Lark, Webhook, OpsGenie, Splunk On-Call, Datadog On-Call
Bot link Telegram
Agents: the Cronitor MCP server tools connect_integration (Slack and PagerDuty), create_integration (browser form for an API key or webhook URL), and list_integrations .
CronitorCLI: cronitor connect <service> --add-to default connects any service and adds it to a notification list. See Using CronitorCLI .
REST: the Integrations API ( integration:read / integration:write ).
To route alerts to an integration, add it to a notification list : the key is the integration's service and the value is its label .
Free plan: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Lark, Telegram, and Webhook. PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Splunk On-Call, and Datadog On-Call need a paid plan.

ABOUT / CRONITOR
We build for developers.
Cronitor builds monitoring tools for developers who care about reliability. When something breaks, we tell you fast with the context needed to fix it.
Where we are today
With five different monitoring tools in one platform, Cronitor helps over 70,000 developers and thousands of teams keep their software running smoothly:
01 Cron job monitoring
02 Website and API monitoring
03 Heartbeat monitoring
04 Website analytics and real user monitoring
05 Hosted status pages
Building tools for developers is what we love doing, and we're grateful for the chance to make your work a little easier.
How it started
Cronitor started in March 2014 with a text message. August, the founding engineer at a logistics startup, had just experienced a critical cron job failing silently.
August texted Shane: “How do you monitor your cron jobs at work?”
Shane was working at a multi-billion dollar company . The answer? They didn't.
We compared notes, looked at what was available, and realized nobody had built something simple that just worked. So we decided to build it ourselves.
A few months later, Cronitor launched on Hacker News . The response told us we weren't the only ones with this problem.
Ten years later
We've stayed independent, grown with our community, and kept building tools we use ourselves every day. Each new feature came from listening to real problems:
2014 Basic cron job monitoring
2016 Uptime monitoring
2017 CronitorCLI: one-command monitoring for cron jobs
2019 Browser-based synthetic monitoring
2020 Kubernetes integration
2022 Status pages
2023 Website analytics and real user monitoring
2025 Cron Dashboard: a visual crontab editor for Linux
2026 MCP server and AI agent monitoring
Over a decade in, we're still passionate about building tools that make developers' lives better. If that resonates with you, we'd love to help.
Thanks to everyone building cool stuff,
August & Shane
